cards.title: Keep it secret
cards.body: Never tell anyone your OTP. A caller or message asking for it may be a scam.

cards.title: A code is for you
cards.body: An OTP can approve a sign-in or payment. Read the screen before you use it.

cards.title: Stop and check
cards.body: If someone rushes you for a code, stop. Contact the bank using its official app or card.

questions.question: Who should know your OTP?
questions.explanation: Keep your OTP private.

questions.question: A caller asks for your code. What do you do?
options: Do not share; stop and check
questions.explanation: A real helper does not need you to tell them your OTP.

questions.question: What can an OTP do?
questions.explanation: An OTP may approve a sign-in or payment.

cards.title: PIN means pay
cards.body: You need your UPI PIN only to PAY. You never need it to RECEIVE money.

cards.title: Keep PIN private
cards.body: Never share your UPI PIN, even with someone who says they are from a bank.

cards.title: Check before paying
cards.body: Read the name and amount on screen before entering your PIN.

questions.question: When do you need a UPI PIN?
questions.explanation: A UPI PIN is used to approve a payment.

questions.question: Someone says “enter PIN to get money.” What is true?
options: You never need a PIN to receive money
questions.explanation: A PIN is only for paying, never for receiving.

questions.question: Before entering your PIN, check what?
questions.explanation: Check who gets the money and how much.

cards.title: Cover the keypad
cards.body: Hide the keypad with your hand when you enter your ATM PIN.

cards.title: Never tell the PIN
cards.body: Bank staff, strangers, and callers must not know your ATM PIN.

cards.title: Use a safe ATM
cards.body: If a stranger offers help or the machine looks changed, cancel and leave.

questions.question: How do you protect your ATM PIN?
questions.explanation: Cover the keypad so others cannot see.

questions.question: A stranger offers to help and asks for your PIN. What do you do?
questions.explanation: Never tell anyone your ATM PIN.

questions.question: The ATM looks changed. What is safest?
questions.explanation: Do not use a machine that looks unsafe.

cards.title: Scan means pay
cards.body: A QR code may start a payment. Check the screen before you approve.

cards.title: PIN does not receive
cards.body: You need a PIN to PAY, never to RECEIVE money.

cards.title: Check the name
cards.body: Before paying, check the person’s name and amount shown on your phone.

cards.title: Buyers and QR codes
cards.body: A buyer on a marketplace says “scan this QR to receive payment”. Scanning a QR only ever SENDS money. To receive money, share only your UPI ID. Never scan, never enter a PIN.

questions.question: What can scanning a QR code do?
questions.explanation: Some QR codes start a payment.

questions.question: A person asks for your PIN to send you money. What should you know?
options: PIN is never needed to receive
questions.explanation: A PIN is only needed to pay.

questions.question: What should you check before approving?
questions.explanation: Check the name and amount on the payment screen.

cards.title: Police do not arrest by video
cards.body: Police or CBI never put you under “digital arrest” over a video call.

cards.title: Do not send money
cards.body: A caller may threaten you and demand money. Do not pay or share codes.

cards.title: Get help safely
cards.body: End the call. Tell someone you trust and report at 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in.

questions.question: Can police put you under digital arrest on a video call?
options: Yes, if the caller is strict
questions.explanation: Police and CBI never do digital arrest over video call.

questions.question: A caller threatens you and asks for money. What do you do?
options: End the call and get help
questions.explanation: Do not send money or share codes under pressure.

questions.question: Where can you report cyber fraud?
questions.explanation: Use 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in.

cards.title: Avoid message links
cards.body: Banks do not ask you to update KYC through a link in a message.

cards.title: Use official ways
cards.body: Open your bank app yourself or visit your bank. Do not use a link sent by a stranger.

cards.title: Never share codes
cards.body: Do not share OTP, PIN, or password to “save” an account.

questions.question: How do banks ask you to update KYC?
options: They do not ask through links
By asking for your PIN in chat
questions.explanation: Banks do not ask KYC updates through links.

questions.question: A text says your account will close; tap a link. What is safer?
questions.explanation: Use the official app or visit your bank.

questions.question: What should you never share?
questions.explanation: Keep OTP and PIN private.

cards.title: Check the order
cards.body: A caller may say a parcel is held. Check with the shop or courier using its official app.

cards.title: Do not install helper apps
cards.body: A courier does not need remote-control access to your phone to deliver a parcel.

cards.title: Do not pay under fear
cards.body: Do not scan a payment QR or share an OTP because of a threat about a parcel.

cards.title: Parcel and police call
cards.body: A call says drugs were found in your parcel and passes you to the “police”. This is a digital arrest scam. No agency arrests anyone on a video call. Hang up and call 1930.

questions.question: A caller says your parcel is held and asks you to install an app. What do you do?
options: Do not install; check the official app
questions.explanation: A delivery does not need remote access to your phone.

questions.question: How can you check a parcel claim?
questions.explanation: Check through a source you open yourself.

questions.question: A parcel caller demands an OTP. What is safe?
questions.explanation: Never share an OTP.

cards.title: Check before installing
cards.body: Use a trusted app store and check who made the loan app.

cards.title: Do not give phone access
cards.body: A loan app should not need your contacts, photos, or messages to lend money.

cards.title: Ask for help
cards.body: If an app threatens you or demands money, save the message and seek help from someone you trust.

cards.title: Fees and harassment
cards.body: A real lender does not ask for a fee before the loan. If callers harass you or message your contacts, do not pay. Save proof and report at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930.

questions.question: Before installing a loan app, what should you check?
questions.explanation: Check the app maker and use a trusted store.

questions.question: An app asks for all your contacts and photos. What is safer?
questions.explanation: Do not give unnecessary access to private information.

questions.question: A loan app threatens you. What can you do?
options: Save the message and seek help
questions.explanation: Keep evidence and seek trusted help.

cards.title: Power cut threat
cards.body: A message says your power will be cut tonight unless you pay or call a number. Do not. Check your bill in the official electricity app.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body: Never share your OTP or PIN. Receiving money never needs a PIN. Call 1930 for help.

questions.question: What do you do?
options: Call the number in the message
Check the official app or office
questions.explanation: Real power companies do not cut supply by a private message.

cards.title: SIM will be blocked
cards.body: A caller says your SIM will be blocked unless you press a key, share a code, or install an app. Hang up. Visit your mobile shop yourself.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body: Never share your OTP or PIN. Receiving money never needs a PIN. Call 1930 for help.

questions.question: What do you do?
options: Share the code to keep the SIM
Hang up and visit the mobile shop
questions.explanation: A SIM swap needs your code. Never give it.

cards.title: Search result numbers
cards.body: A number found in a search or on a social post may be a fake customer care line. Use the number in the official app or on your card.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body: Never share your OTP or PIN. Receiving money never needs a PIN. Call 1930 for help.

questions.question: Where do you get a help number?
options: The official app or your card
questions.explanation: Fake helpers ask you to install an app or approve a payment.

cards.title: A request takes money
cards.body: A collect request asks YOU to pay. If someone says "approve to receive money", it is a trick. Decline it.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body: Never share your OTP or PIN. Receiving money never needs a PIN. Call 1930 for help.

questions.question: A stranger says "approve and enter PIN to get money". What is true?
questions.explanation: A PIN is only for paying. Decline the request.

cards.title: Pay first, earn later
cards.body: Part-time task jobs, like-and-review work, trading or crypto groups that promise sure profit are traps. Real jobs do not ask you to pay first.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body: Never share your OTP or PIN. Receiving money never needs a PIN. Call 1930 for help.

questions.question: A group promises guaranteed returns if you deposit money. What is it?
questions.explanation: No one can guarantee profit. Stop and tell someone you trust.

cards.title: Do not pay, do not delete
cards.body: If someone threatens to share private photos or a video call recording, stay calm. This is not your fault. Do not pay. Do not delete the chats. Tell someone you trust and report at cybercrime.gov.in.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body: Never share your OTP or PIN. Receiving money never needs a PIN. Call 1930 for help.

questions.question: Someone threatens you with a private video. What do you do?
options: Do not pay, keep chats, report
questions.explanation: Paying brings more demands. Keep the proof and report.

cards.title: You did not enter
cards.body: A message says you won a lottery, a quiz prize or a gift. If you never entered, it is fake. Real prizes never ask for a fee or a PIN.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body: Never share your OTP or PIN. Receiving money never needs a PIN. Call 1930 for help.

questions.question: You "won" a prize but must pay a fee first. What is it?
questions.explanation: A prize that asks for money first is a scam.

cards.title: Call them back
cards.body: A voice or message says a relative is in trouble and needs money now, from a new number. Hang up. Call the relative back on their OLD number.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body: Never share your OTP or PIN. Receiving money never needs a PIN. Call 1930 for help.

questions.question: A "relative" on a new number asks for money. First step?
options: Call them on their old number
questions.explanation: Also ask for the family code from the app Family screen. A scammer will not know it.

cards.title: Look before you tap
cards.body: Be careful with shortened links, links made of numbers, misspelt bank names and links starting with xn--. Do not tap them. Open the official app yourself.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body: Never share your OTP or PIN. Receiving money never needs a PIN. Call 1930 for help.

questions.question: You get a link about your bank account. What do you do?
questions.explanation: Typing or opening the official app is always safer than a link.
